7.3 Locking Device when the Container is StationaryClass B Container with Four Castors - Each Class B container shall include a locking device when it is stationary, or possibly an optional locking, and shall satisfy the tests defined in IS : 12402 ( Part 2)-1988 `Mobile containers for solid waste: In case where locking acts upon the castors, it shall act at the Part 2 Methods of test' ( under print). minimum upon two adjacent castors. 7.4 Plugged Outlet for Washing and Draining - Class B Container with Four Castors - Each Class B container shall include a plugged outlet for washing and draining lccated at the lowest point on the container body. The minimum diameter of a plugged outlet shall be 40 mm. It shall be easily accessible. 7.4.1 For Class A containers, this device is optional.

7.5 Control Device for the Purpose of Towage - Class B Container with Four Castors - This device is optional and shall be arranged by mutual agreement between the customer and the supplier. 7.6 Wheels and Castors Metal parts shall be 7.6.1 C/ass A containers - The two wheels of Class A container are fixed. corrosion resistant and satisfy the tests specified in IS : 12402 ( Part 2 )-1988. EXPLANATORY
This standard is destined drawing up of their contracts. for local communities to

NOTE
be used as a reference document in the

It enables all types of mechanical handling, conforming to the standard, to be used for all types of containers also defined in the standard, in order to take into account the existing container depot on one hand and on the other the non-centralization of purchases in the case of a group of communities ( see Note ).
Note - It is the mayor of each `commune' who, within the scope of his policing powers and in application of the region's health regulations, defines the conditions under which household refuse must be prepared for collection; he, therefore, determines rhe type of container required for his `commune'.

In the case of a communal service, where choices are not divided and where the existing depot is centralized, the persons incharge may opt for one of the two gripping systems defined in this standard. In the case of an urban community, a district or a group of `commune' it is the deliberative organization who decides on the purchasing of buckets and hence on the choice of the gripping system. This standard is being issued in the following Part 1 General characteristics Part 2 Methods of test two parts:

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from French Standard NFH 96-1 IO-1 982 `Mobile containers for solid waste - General characteristics' issued by the L' Association Francaise de Normalisation (AFNOR ). 6
